newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 18.

text.p: The government would ask for a debate on Aotearoa Television Network in Parliament this afternoon to force opposition MPs to reveal any evidence of wrongdoing, Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Monday. Parliament resumed today after more than nine weeks, and the sitting is expected to be a "bloody" affair as opposition parties take advantage of a long-awaited opportunity to grill the Coalition Government. Page 1.

Public and school summer holidays should be rescheduled later in January to reduce Christmas stress, Women's Affairs Minister Chris Fletcher said on Monday. Fletcher said if schools worked till Christmas or even into January, there would be less Christmas stress for women and families. Page 1.

Tukoroirangi Morgan will front up with his constituents, the NZ First caucus and Parliament over his role in the Aotearoa Television fiasco. Morgan will be pressed to explain why he and fellow Aotearoa Television director Morehu McDonald spent thousands of dollars of the Maori television station's money on
clothing, including an $89 pair of underpants bought by Morgan. Page 2.

Australian Prime Minister John Howard stepped up pressure on Monday on New Zealand to increase its defence spending, choosing a Beehive press conference to announce that Australia for the second year running would not cut its defence budget. The press conference followed a meeting with the Cabinet at which, sources said, Howard made clear that Australia believed new Zealand was not maintaining the "credible minimum" defence force it said it would. Page 2.

The Labour Party plans to introduce to Parliament a bill allowing a six-week paid parental leave period. Women's affairs spokeswoman Dianne Yates said on Monday that the bill was intended to bring legislation into line with that of other Western Countries. Page 2.

Telecom Corporation shares took another blow on Monday, falling five cents to $6.86, as the market continued its nervous wait for the third-quarter profit result, due this morning. The shares traded as low as $6.76 during the day before bouncing

back. Brokers have picked a quarterly result as low as $170 million, up to $188 million. The Telecom share price has fallen about ten percent in the past few weeks from a recent high of $7.60, as word has spread that the profit result may not be as good as earlier expected. Page 10.

Retail sales data showing the pre-Christmas period was even tougher than expected is being treated by financial markets as only neutral. Seasonally and price-adjusted retail sales fell 0.1 percent in the December quarter, against a general market expectation of a rise of about 0.2 percent. The footwear sector
was again the largest loser, with a fifth consecutive quarter of negative growth. Page 10.

Whiteware maker Fisher and Paykel's Australian market share has soared since 1991, and retailers and consumers now see it as one of the top manufacturers, a survey by leading Australian market researcher and forecaster BIS Shrapnel has found. Survey project manager Ruth O'Grady said Fisher and Paykel was always ranked in the middle-to-top ranks among suppliers. Page 10.

Hotel operator Kingsgate International reported on Monday a bottom-line profit of $2.56 million in the year to December 1996, turning around a $807,000 loss in the previous year. Total revenue was up 16.6 percent at $37.53 million. No tax was paid in either period and no dividend was declared. Page 10.

Southland Farmers directors have agreed in principle to a merger of the company's stock and station business with Dunedin-based Reid Farmers. The offer, for an undisclosed sum, depends on Reid Farmers satisfactorily completing due diligence before April 30. Page 10.

Union Shipping says it will withdraw from the trans-Tasman Shipping Consortium on February 28 and instead operate as an independent carrier across the Tasman. The consortium comprises Tasman Express Line, P and O Nedlloyd and Union Shipping. Union Shipping and Australia New Zealand Direct plan to merge on March 1, subject to regulatory approval. Page 10.
